title: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the …
body: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the edited bullet exits non-zero]) is structurally vacuous: line 901 contains zero path tokens, so the loop body never executes and the oracle passes with zero iterations. The intent (no gitignored path token in the bullet) is satisfied, but a zero-match sweep passing silently is the same self-nullifying shape the bullet at patterns.md:901 warns about. Consider asserting a non-zero token count before iterating.

title: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` …
body: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` and `$c:s` are path modifiers, so a loop written as `git show "$c:test/foo.ts"` silently expands to `<sha>est/foo.ts` and, with stderr redirected, yields an empty file and a bogus `grep -c` of 0 for every commit. This produced two wrong measurements during this review and is the unidentified cause of the 'for-loop pipeline gave inconsistent readings' note in the round-2 artifact. Per-commit sweeps should run under an explicit `bash -c`.

title: hasFrozenIntegerComparand excuses EVERY integer comparand in a command as soon …
body: hasFrozenIntegerComparand excuses EVERY integer comparand in a command as soon as ANY live-derivation token appears anywhere in that command. A mixed oracle such as `test $(git show main:f | wc -l) -ge 1 && test $(wc -l < g) -eq 42` hides the frozen 42 behind the unrelated live token. Again this matches the PRD notes ('when NO live re-derivation token appears in the SAME criterion'), so it is spec-conformant; a per-comparand scoping would be strictly stronger and is worth a follow-up.

title: Test named 'does not match main by literal substring -- mainbranch is not the m…
body: Test named 'does not match main by literal substring -- mainbranch is not the main token' lives inside the 'frozen-comparand rule: flagged forms' describe and asserts not.toBeNull(). The assertion is correct (mainbranch must not count as a live main token, so the criterion IS flagged), but the 'does not match' phrasing reads as a negative/passing case and momentarily inverts the reader's expectation. Consider renaming to something like 'flags a mainbranch: ref, which is not the main token'.

title: Doc comment states the guard must 'precede' the sed anchor ('no test -n "$VAR" …
body: Doc comment states the guard must 'precede' the sed anchor ('no test -n "$VAR" / [ -n "$VAR" ] guard for that exact variable name precedes it anywhere in the command'), but hasUnguardedSedLineAnchor applies guardRe to the whole command string with no positional constraint, so a guard appearing AFTER the anchor also suppresses the finding. The behavior is the more permissive of the two and is defensible; the comment should be reworded to match it (per the project lesson that a comment does not prove runtime behavior).
